------
1. Hareram Sahu 2. Rajendra Sahu .... .... .... Petitioners Versus The State of Jharkhand .... .... .... Opposite Party ------
CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR CHOUDHARY ------
For the Petitioners : Mr. Rishu Ranjan, Advocate
For the State : Mr. Satish Prasad, Addl.

P.P  For the Informant : Mr. Rohit Sinha, Advocate  ------
 Order No.11 Dated- 18/08/2023  Heard the parties.

Apprehending their arrest, the petitioners have moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail in connection with Chutia P.S. Case No.15 of 2021 registered under Sections 406 &
420 of the Indian Penal Code.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the informant entered into an agreement for sell of a land with the co-accused Binu Sahu who is the power of attorney holder of the owner of the land namely Gobardhan Sahu and Pushpa Devi but the said Gobardhan Sahu and Pushpa Devi subsequently revoked the said power of attorney executed in favour of Binu Sahu and the allegation against the petitioners is that the petitioners are the sons of Gobardhan Sahu and Pushpa Devi and a sum of Rs.4,50,000/- has been transferred to the account of petitioner No.1 namely Hareram Sahu and a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- has been transferred to the account of the petitioner No.2 namely Rajendra Sahu.
It is submitted that the allegations against the petitioner are all false.
It is then submitted that the dispute between the parties is purely a civil dispute.

It is next submitted that the petitioners are ready and willing to pay Rs.4,50,000/- and Rs.2,00,000/- respectively to the informant without prejudice to their defence in this case and undertake to cooperate with the investigation of the case and they have file an affidavit to this effect, in this anticipatory bail Hareram Sahu vs The State Of Jharkhand .... .... .... ... on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147638173/

sentences.text:
It is also submitted that the co-accused, with similar allegations, have already been given the privileges of anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 09.07.2021 passed in A.B.A.
No.4254 of 2021.
Hence, it is submitted that on the principle of parity, the petitioners be also given the privileges of anticipatory bail.
Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State being assisted by the learned counsel for the informant vehemently oppose the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioners.
Considering the submissions of the counsels and the fact as discussed above, I am of the opinion that it is a fit case where the above named petitioners be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Hence, in the event of their arrest or surrender within a period of six weeks from the date of this order, they shall be released on bail on petitioner No.1 depositing a demand draft of Rs.4,50,000/-
drawn in favour of informant without prejudice to his defence in this case, petitioner No.2 depositing a demand draft of Rs.2,00,000/- drawn in favour of informant without prejudice to his defence in this case and both of them on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi in connection with Chutia P.S. Case No.15 of 2021 with the condition that the petitioners will cooperate with the investigation of the case and appear before the Investigating Officer as and when noticed by him and will furnish their mobile number and a copy of their Aadhar Card in the court below with the undertaking that they will not change their mobile number during the pendency of the case and subject to the conditions laid down under section 438 (2) Cr. P.C.
In case, the petitioners deposit the amount, the court below is directed to issue notice to the informant and hand over the said demand draft to him, after proper identification.

(Anil Kumar Choudhary, J.) Animesh/
